neighbours.label: the subject of an 'if' clause stating a condition for a goal ('necessary if we', later 'are to'), not ordinary conditionals or other subordinate subjects
fire: Farmers will need far better forecasts if they are to protect their crops from drought.
Serious investment is essential if our hospitals are to cope with the coming winter.
Trust has to be rebuilt if the two communities are to live side by side again.
Much more must be done if we hope to halve emissions by the end of the decade.
Patience is required if one wishes to master the violin as an adult.
These reforms are vital if young people are to find decent work in the region.
Parents need clear guidance if they are to help their children read at home.
New rules must be adopted if the fishing industry is to survive the next decade.
quiet: Farmers will sell their crops at the market on Friday if they finish the harvest early.
Our hospitals are quite busy, and I wonder if they have a bed free tonight.
The two communities held a street party, and nobody knew if they would do it again.
Call me on Sunday if we win the match, and I will bring a cake round.
You can borrow my violin if one of yours breaks during the concert.
These young people said that they found decent work after moving to the region.
Parents told the teacher that they read with their children at home most evenings.
The fishing boats stayed in the harbour since they had heard the storm warning.

notes: Card: ' they', ' we', ' students', ' one' after 'must ... if'; the + pole is ' going' and promotes ' to', so both poles relate to an upcoming 'to'. Probes: 0.25-0.30 for the pattern, plain conditionals and 'that we' under 0.06.
